# Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling

Also called: Dynamic NeRF, 4D NeRF, Temporal NeRF

## Overview
Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling extends static Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) to handle video sequences and time-varying scenes by introducing a temporal dimension $t$ into the radiance field representation [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. It solves the problem of reconstructing dynamic content, which standard NeRF cannot represent, by allowing density and color to vary over time [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. Unlike static methods, it explicitly models scene dynamics, either through direct time conditioning, deformation fields, or particle systems [13848-gear-nerf.md][15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md][15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md][15551-kfd-nerf.md].

## Shared principles
The standard NeRF architecture [Parent](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md) serves as the baseline. The primary modification is the input expansion to include time $t$ alongside spatial position $\mathbf{x}$ and view direction $\mathbf{d}$ [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. The volume rendering equation is adapted to integrate over time-dependent density $\sigma(\mathbf{x}, t)$ and color $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}, t)$ [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]:

$$
C(\mathbf{r}, t) = \int_{s_n}^{s_f} T(s, t) \sigma(\mathbf{r}(s), t) \mathbf{c}(\mathbf{r}(s), \mathbf{d}, t) ds
$$

where $\mathbf{r}(s) = \mathbf{o} + s\mathbf{d}$ is the ray equation and $T(s, t)$ is the accumulated transmittance at time $t$ [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. Time $t$ is typically processed using positional encoding $\gamma_t(t)$ similar to spatial coordinates [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md].

## Subtopics

### [Gear-NeRF](13848-gear-nerf.md)
Gear-NeRF stratifies a 4D scene into discrete "gear" levels based on semantic motion scales, assigning higher-resolution feature volumes to regions with larger motion [13848-gear-nerf.md]. It differs from [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md) by using discrete levels to allocate computational resources proportional to motion intensity, and from [KFD-NeRF](15551-kfd-nerf.md) by using semantic embeddings rather than explicit deformation fields [13848-gear-nerf.md]. Choose this method when motion varies significantly across different semantic regions of the scene.

### [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md)
This method adapts standard NeRF by introducing $t$ as a direct input to the MLP, allowing density and color to vary over time [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. It relies solely on input expansion without explicit deformation fields [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. It is the simplest baseline for dynamic scenes but suffers from blurriness and ghosting artifacts due to the lack of explicit motion modeling [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md].

### [Forward Warping for Novel View Synthesis](15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md)
This method models a static scene at a canonical time step and forward warps the radiance field to other times using a deformation field and differentiable splatting [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md]. It addresses many-to-one mapping difficulties inherent in dynamic reconstruction [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md]. It differs from backward flow methods by leveraging a canonical representation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on public datasets [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md].

### [Dynamic Appearance Particle Neural Radiance Field](15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md)
This method integrates a particle-based motion network with a static grid-based radiance field to model dynamic scenes from monocular video [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md]. It solves the multi-view constraint of methods like ParticleNeRF by applying appearance particles only to dynamic elements [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md]. It differs from ParticleNeRF by using a grid-based field with linear interpolation for efficient querying [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md].

### [KFD-NeRF](15551-kfd-nerf.md)
KFD-NeRF models the 4D radiance field as a dynamic system estimated using a Kalman filter, combining observations from input data with predictions from local linear motion equations [15551-kfd-nerf.md]. It explicitly separates motion estimation into an observer branch and a predictor branch, fusing them via a learnable Kalman gain [15551-kfd-nerf.md]. It uses deformation fields warped to a canonical space represented by tri-planes, enabling smoother learning than feature-interpolation approaches [15551-kfd-nerf.md].

## Background
The standard NeRF architecture [Parent](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md) was originally designed for static scenes. Extensions to dynamic scenes emerged to handle video data, with methods ranging from simple time-conditioned MLPs [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md] to complex deformation and particle-based systems [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md][15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md][15551-kfd-nerf.md]. These methods address the limitations of static representations in video sequences, such as ghosting and blurriness [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md].
